kill_fact: No outright kill - the deal is real, binding and alive, so the arb thesis survives. Verified against primary sources: C$44.00/share all-cash arrangement (~C$5.5B) announced 2026-01-26 on Allied's IR site; shareholders approved 99.54% of votes cast at the 2026-03-31 special meeting; Investment Canada Act approval RECEIVED, ECOWAS + COMESA merger clearances RECEIVED; outside date extended once May 29 -> July 29, 2026 (company PR 2026-05-29); both parties publicly recommitted to closing by July 29 as recently as 2026-06-10. The spread is genuine (~+31% off the true live). BUT two load-bearing legs of the bear-side framing failed verification. (1) WRONG GATE: the bear attacks African host-country lag (Mali/Cote d'Ivoire/Ethiopia/Egypt 'sign-off lags'); the actual binding outstanding condition is China's own outbound-investment approval - a DAY-ONE closing condition ('regulatory approvals in various jurisdictions globally including the People's Republic of China', 2026-01-26 PR) that the entire debate record never mentions - and per FT reporting (2026-05-29) the NDRC has DELAYED it, questioning the 27% premium itself and Mali political risk (~half of Allied's output). A buyer-side regulator balking at the PRICE is renegotiation/quiet-lapse risk, not administrative lag; the July 29 DATE is hard but the door is soft. (2) FLOOR BROKEN: the US$23 floor explicitly 'leans on gold staying strong' - gold is now ~US$4,076/oz, roughly -28% from the 52-week peak (~$5,627) and below both the 50-day (~$4,361) and 200-day (~$4,307) averages; the unaffected price (~C$34.65, the 27%-premium reference) was struck near peak gold in January. A break re-rate in TODAY'S tape lands materially below US$23 (gold producers lever the gold price; TSX 52-wk low C$15.69 ~= US$11), so the claimed 2.8:1 asymmetry compresses toward ~1:1. Thesis survives as a live, mostly-approved cash arb - but with the risk re-labeled and the cushion largely gone.
corrections: (1) REMAINING GATE MISIDENTIFIED (load-bearing): the outstanding approval is PRC/NDRC outbound-investment clearance - delayed per FT 2026-05-29 over the premium and Mali risk - not African host-country paperwork ('obtained or in advanced stages' per the company). The May 29 extension traces to the Chinese impasse. Additionally, late-June media reports flag Mali government approval/permit complications for Zijin assuming control of the Malian assets (Sadiola ~half of output, junta-ruled, active insurgency). (2) FLOOR INVALID AS STATED: sop_bear's US$23 floor is anchored to a 'strong 2026 gold tape' that no longer exists (gold ~$4,076 vs ~$5,627 peak, below 50/200-dma). Off the true live of US$23.71, the market-implied math exposes it: if the floor were really US$23, the price would imply <10% close odds for a 99.5%-approved, thrice-cleared deal five weeks from the outside date - absurd; the market is pricing a break floor well below US$23. Realistic break downside is roughly US$16-19 (-25/-35%), not -US$0.7. (3) STALE NUMBERS: working live 25.26 is stale - NYSE line US$23.71 (2026-07-01/02); C$44.00 converts to ~US$30.97 at spot USDCAD 1.421, not US$31.5. Corrected reward/risk is roughly +7.3 vs -5 to -7, near 1-1.5:1, not 2.8:1. (4) NO REVERSE BREAK FEE: the only disclosed termination amount is C$220M payable BY ALLIED to Zijin; nothing compensates Allied holders if Chinese approval never arrives, and a further extension past July 29 requires MUTUAL agreement - an unenthusiastic NDRC hands Zijin a no-fault exit by simply not agreeing. (5) TIMELINE: expected close at announcement was 'late April 2026'; it has already slipped ~3 months. Catalyst tag should read: date-hard, gate-soft.
evidence: Allied Gold IR press release 2026-01-26 (alliedgold.com): C$44.00/share all-cash, ~C$5.5B, 27% premium to 30-day VWAP as of 2026-01-23; closing conditions include 'applicable competition and regulatory approvals in various jurisdictions globally including the People's Republic of China'; C$220M termination fee payable by Allied Gold in specified circumstances (no reverse fee disclosed); expected close 'late April 2026'

Allied Gold press releases via SEC Form 6-K / GlobeNewswire: 2026-03-31 special meeting - 99.54% of votes cast in favour (99.42% excluding interested persons; 61.14% turnout); 2026-05-29 - Investment Canada Act approval received (completes Canada), ECOWAS + COMESA clearances received, African host-country approvals 'either been obtained or are in advanced stages', Outside Date extended to July 29, 2026, further extension requires mutual agreement; 2026-06-10 - 'both parties remain fully committed to fulfilling the conditions for completion of the Arrangement by the extended outside date of July 29, 2026', Sadiola (Mali) operating normally
